claims.text: Introducing a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation can improve the wear resistance of a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix.
The proposed intervention creates a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation.
Intrinsically nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates provide multi-type adaptive friction-interface protection.
The cooperative nanohierarchical structure releases gradient frictional stress through multiple deformation pathways during room-temperature wear.
At 800 °C, the architecture activates a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer that minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear.
The modified FeNiCrCoCu coating will have better wear resistance than the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating under identical conditions.
The wear-resistance prediction applies from room temperature to 800 °C.
The wear-resistance prediction applies from low to high friction velocities.
The wear-resistance prediction applies from shallow to deep wear depths.
The exact magnitude of the wear-resistance improvement is uncertain.
The optimal composition-undulation parameters remain uncertain.
Comparative sliding tests measuring wear rate, friction coefficient, and microscopic deformation behavior can test the hypothesis.
Failure of the modified coating to show a significantly lower wear rate than the unchanged coating under identical conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
